source: CARE Cambodia (Pailin), "TIP Training on Maize Production" / បទដ្ឋានអនុវត្ដបច្ចេកវិទ្យា ផលិតកម្មដំណំពូតក្របម, 2009. Funded by AusAID (ACIMA project), the European Union (Pailin Food Security Program), and ACIAR (CCPMP project).
text:
The source refers to this herbicide as "ដោខ្វត", locally called "ទឹកសៀវ" in the Pailin area; the product photo in the source shows a label listing paraquat dichloride as the active ingredient. It is a non-selective, contact-type herbicide that kills essentially any plant type it directly touches — grasses, corn, beans, potato and other weeds alike — without regard to species.

Timing and method: it is applied after weeds have already germinated and grown, sprayed directly onto weed leaves/stems so it thoroughly wets the whole weed plant for best effect. Spray must not be allowed to drift onto or contact the crop, since it will kill or damage any part of the crop it touches and reduce yield.

Toxicity: it is highly toxic while active, but becomes inactive once it contacts soil. Clean water (not muddy water) must be used for mixing, since dirty water reduces effectiveness.

Rainfastness: it becomes rain-fast very quickly — rain falling as little as 30 minutes after spraying will not wash off or reduce the chemical's effect, in contrast to glyphosate which needs 4-6 hours.
